description: BFT quorum consensus decision-core golden vectors — the shared seed for cross-language agreement (F#/C#/TS/Rust). From src/Core/Consensus.fs. quorumThreshold(n) = 2*floor((n-1)/3)+1 (the classic 2f+1 BFT quorum for n=3f+1). decide(votes) groups the vote VALUES by value, takes the highest support, and commits it iff that support reaches quorumThreshold(total-vote-count); else rejects with the best support seen. TIE-BREAK = ORDINAL MINIMUM of the values sharing the highest support — order-INDEPENDENT by construction, so two nodes that received the same votes in different orders decide identically. (It was first-occurrence until 2026-08-15, which read arrival ORDER and made nodes diverge wherever a tie can also reach quorum, i.e. exactly n in {2,3,6}. All seven pre-existing vectors below are UNCHANGED by that fix — first-occurrence and ordinal-minimum agree on every one of them, which is why the old rule was never actually pinned. The last four decide vectors are the discriminators added with the fix: first-occurrence gets each of them WRONG, giving 'r', 'b', 'b' and 'a' respectively.) Ordinal, never culture-sensitive (.claude/rules/culture-invariant-by-default.md): the ['a','Z'] vector commits 'Z' because U+005A precedes U+0061 by codepoint, though most linguistic collations order them the other way. Known residual, named not pinned: F#/C#/TS compare by UTF-16 code unit and Rust by UTF-8 byte, so the oracles disagree on a tie straddling the astral/high-BMP boundary; every value in this seed is ASCII, where all four agree. The vote state machine (transition) carries timestamps and is out of byte-lock scope. result: {committed, value (null on reject), count, total}.
